    LogAlerts
    Alerts (sometimes called errors or status events elsewhere) are for reporting problems with the logging system itself rather than application logging - for example an appender failing to write, or an async publisher's queue overflowing.
    LogAlerts.Listener
    Notified of alerts as they happen.
    LogAlerts.Stats
    Stats about alerts recorded.
    LogAlerts.UnobservedErrorsAction
    What LogLifecycle.start(LogConfig) does if, at that moment, at least one alert has been recorded and still zero LogAlerts.Listeners are registered - the situation Logback's StatusManager calls an unobserved status: nothing is watching, so whatever went wrong during property loading or a RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator would otherwise only ever have reached the individual, easy to miss stderr lines each LogAlerts.error(LogEvent) call already produces.

    A dynamic version of LogEvent's static "of" factory methods - same method shapes (level, message, ...), but LogEventFactory.timestamp(), LogEventFactory.threadName(), LogEventFactory.threadId() and LogEventFactory.loggerName() are resolved through overridable methods instead of being passed in on every call/pulled from Instant.now()/Thread.currentThread() inline the way those static methods do.

    Metrics are cheap, numeric counters about the logging system itself - for example how many events an appender has dropped, or how often a reused encoder buffer had to shrink itself back down.

    A log properties that can be mutated like a map.

    Mutable Log properties builder.
    LogProperties.StandardProperties
    Common static log properties such as System properties ane environment variables.
    LogProperty
    Describes a key (or several fallback keys) resolved against a LogProperties instance - start with LogProperties.forKey(String) - and also serves as the namespace for the shared property machinery: LogProperty.Result, LogProperty.Validator, and the property-specific exceptions.
    LogProperty.PropertyConvertException
    Thrown if an error happens while converting a property.
    LogProperty.PropertyFunction
    An error friendly Function for converting properties.
    LogProperty.PropertyMissingException
    Throw if property is missing.
    LogProperty.PropertyProblem
    Parent interface for property exceptions.
    LogProperty.PropertySupport
    Property helper mixin.
    LogProperty.RequiredResult
    A result that is not missing and will either be an error or success.
    LogProperty.Result
    The result of a property fetched from properties.
    LogProperty.Result.Error
    A property that was present but failed conversion.
    LogProperty.Result.Missing
    A property that is missing (null).
    LogProperty.Result.Success
    A property that is present.
    LogProperty.ValidatedResult
    A LogProperty.Result that is safe to pull a value out of - either because it can never actually be missing (LogProperty.RequiredResult: a LogProperty.Result.Success or an LogProperty.Result.Error, both already resolved one way or the other) or because a caller has explicitly acknowledged the possibility of a still-LogProperty.Result.Missing result by running it through LogProperty.Result.validate(Validator), LogProperty.Result.validateIfError(Validator), or LogProperty.Result.validateNow(Class).
    LogProperty.ValidationException
    Thrown by LogProperty.Validator.validate() when one or more of the accumulated LogProperty.Results failed, reporting every failure in a single message instead of just the first one encountered.
    LogProperty.Validator
    Accumulates LogProperty.Results from one or more property lookups and validates them together, so that a caller resolving several properties in sequence can report every failure at once instead of failing fast on the first bad property.
